title: [Android] CameraX preview is rotated 90 degrees
body: After upgrading to camera 0.11.0+2, which resolves to camera_android_camerax 0.6.8+3, the Android camera preview is rotated by 90 degrees on my Pixel 1. The same code worked with camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2. I see the problem with the regular Skia renderer and also when trying Impeller. CameraPreview should display the preview in the correct orientation without application-specific rotation corrections.

symptoms_visible: On a Pixel 1, CameraPreview displays the live Android camera image rotated by 90 degrees after upgrading from camera_android_camerax 0.6.7+2 to a later version.
N0.label: N0 rotated CameraX preview reported

symptoms_visible: The Pixel 1 preview remains rotated on package versions containing the earlier Impeller-related fix, both with the regular Skia renderer and when Impeller is requested.
N1_x.label: N1_x prior-fix duplicate aftermath

symptoms_visible: The preview is always incorrectly oriented on both a real Pixel 1 and its API 29 emulator, while an older Samsung API 22 device displays the same preview correctly.
Changing between the available Skia and Impeller configurations does not remove the Pixel 1 rotation.
N2.label: N2 device and renderer comparison collected

symptoms_visible: Affected phones and tablets from several manufacturers show a live preview that is sideways, upside down, or stretched, although the captured photo may display normally.
On some devices the initial preview is correct but becomes wrong in one landscape direction; on others, starting the app while already in landscape reliably produces an incorrect preview.
Naturally landscape-oriented tablets can show the preview rotated by 180 degrees in every device orientation.
N3.label: N3 orientation-dependent cross-device reproductions

symptoms_visible: With camera_android_camerax 0.6.9 or later, the previously sideways preview becomes correct on several API 29 devices.
Other devices still show an incorrect preview when the app starts in landscape, when auto-rotate is locked, or on naturally landscape-oriented hardware.
N4.label: N4 API 29 partial correction measured

symptoms_visible: Wrapping CameraPreview in a fixed quarter-turn RotatedBox can make one portrait view look correct, but the preview becomes incorrectly oriented again after the device rotates or on devices requiring a different correction.
N4_x.label: N4_x manual quarter-turn aftermath

symptoms_visible: Tests that merely remove the plugin rotation or switch rendering backends produce inconsistent orientations across real phones and tablets.
During debugging, the calculated orientation changes while the displayed preview can remain at its previous angle.
N5.label: N5 runtime rotation causes isolated

symptoms_visible: With camera_android_camerax 0.6.14, affected real phones and tablets display the live preview in the expected orientation while the device orientation changes.
Multiple affected users confirm that the package fix works without their previous manual preview rotation.
N6.label: N6 released package verified by affected users

symptoms_visible: The runtime-aware preview rotation fix is available in camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 and affected users have verified correct previews on real devices.
N_terminal.label: terminal resolved

solution.intent: Treat the report as a duplicate of the earlier Impeller preview-rotation issue and ask the reporter to use the latest Flutter main branch containing that fix.
solution.concrete_example: This appears to be the same as issue #149294, which is fixed on main; switch to the latest main channel and retry.

edges.comment: The issue was initially closed as a duplicate. The reporter showed that the failure occurs on versions already containing that fix and with both Skia and Impeller configurations, so it was reopened.

question_patterns: Can you reproduce this on an emulator with the same Android version as the Pixel 1?
What Android API level is the affected Pixel 1 running?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The real Pixel 1 runs Android API 29, and a Pixel 1 emulator configured with the API 29 system image behaves exactly the same: its preview is always incorrectly oriented.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Pixel 1 emulator is correct, and only one damaged physical device shows the problem.
The same API 29 reproduction is obtained with a different Pixel 1 emulator image.

question_patterns: Does the same sample work on another Android device?
Can you check a non-Pixel device?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: An old Samsung running Android 5.1.1/API 22 displays the preview correctly with the same sample.

question_patterns: Does enabling or disabling Impeller change the result?
Is the issue limited to the Impeller renderer?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. The issue occurs with the regular Skia renderer, and trying to enable Impeller gives the same result; the Pixel 1 does not appear to support Impeller normally.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview is correct with Skia and rotates only when Impeller is enabled.

edges.comment: The reporter's comparisons falsify the original duplicate diagnosis and establish a reproducible API/device-dependent preview problem.

question_patterns: Which other devices show an incorrect live preview?
Is the problem limited to the Pixel 1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is not limited to the Pixel 1. Reports include Xiaomi, Samsung, Realme, OnePlus, Pixel emulators and several tablets. The live CameraX preview can be rotated and stretched, while a photo shown after capture is correctly oriented and not stretched.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Only recorded-video playback is rotated; the live CameraPreview is correct on every device.
The affected applications use different colors for their capture buttons.

question_patterns: Does the device orientation at startup affect the preview?
What happens when the app starts while the device is already in landscape or auto-rotate is locked?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Starting the app after locking the device in landscape reproduces the issue reliably. On a Pixel 3A emulator, rotating 90 degrees to the right is wrong while rotating left can be correct. A Pixel 5 started in landscape is off by 180 degrees in one direction and by 90 degrees in the other.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The initial orientation and subsequent device rotations never affect the result; only the selected camera lens matters.
The wrong direction is landscape left rather than landscape right, but startup orientation still controls the failure.

question_patterns: Can this be reproduced on a naturally landscape-oriented tablet?
Is the incorrect rotation consistent on tablets?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. Pixel Tablet, Samsung Galaxy Tab and other landscape-oriented devices reproduce it. Some show a preview rotated 180 degrees in every orientation, while others display a portrait preview when held in landscape.

question_patterns: Is the captured photo also rotated, or only the live preview?
Does viewing the captured image reproduce the same stretch and rotation?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The live preview is rotated or stretched, but the captured photo can look correct when displayed separately. Rotated recorded-video playback is a separate issue tracked elsewhere.

edges.comment: Reports from all affected participants are folded into one simulated user side. The evidence distinguishes this live CameraPreview defect from recorded-video playback and image-metadata issues.

question_patterns: Can you test camera_android_camerax 0.6.9 with a dependency override?
Does the package containing the API 29 boundary correction fix the original preview?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes for the common API 29 case. The 0.6.9 override fixes the rotated live preview on the original class of affected devices, including a Huawei API 29 report and several Redmi devices.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Version 0.6.9 leaves the original Pixel 1/API 29 preview rotated exactly as before.

question_patterns: After the API 29 fix, does the preview remain correct in every orientation and when the app starts in landscape?
Please test portrait, both landscape directions, auto-rotate off, and startup while already in landscape.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. Portrait can be correct while both landscape directions remain wrong; with auto-rotate off the orientations may be inverted. Starting the app while already in landscape also still reproduces the problem on newer devices.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The preview remains correct in portrait, both landscape directions, with auto-rotate disabled, and when launched in landscape.
Only landscape right remains wrong instead of both landscape directions.

edges.comment: Testing 0.6.9 is a handler-requested package-version probe. It demonstrates that correcting the API 29 cutoff addressed many reports but was only a partial fix.

solution.intent: Work around the plugin by wrapping CameraPreview in a fixed RotatedBox and adjusting its aspect ratio in application code.
solution.concrete_example: Wrap CameraPreview with RotatedBox(quarterTurns: 1) and an AspectRatio based on cameraController.value.aspectRatio.

edges.comment: A fixed RotatedBox visibly corrected one portrait case, but participants immediately showed that it fails after rotation and differs across devices and platforms. It is not a general resolution.

question_patterns: Can you test the candidate preview changes with Vulkan, OpenGLES and Skia on real devices?
Does removing the plugin's rotation correction solve the issue consistently?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: No. Removing the correction fixes some cases but rotates previously correct devices such as a physical Pixel 7 by 90 degrees. Samsung phones and tablets remain wrong under Vulkan, OpenGLES and Skia in some tests, so selecting behavior solely from the renderer or deleting all correction is not reliable.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Removing all plugin rotation logic fixes every tested real device and backend without regressions.
The same inconsistent device results occur, but OpenGLES and Vulkan labels are reversed in one log.

edges.comment: Cross-device candidate testing ruled out a renderer-name-only fix. Engineer debugging then isolated two interacting plugin defects: orientation events did not rebuild the Texture-based preview, and API level was only an unreliable estimate of whether the SurfaceProducer already handled crop and rotation.

question_patterns: Can you test camera_android_camerax 0.6.14 on the real devices that previously showed the rotated preview?
Does the released runtime-aware preview fix work without your manual RotatedBox workaround?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. The fix works on affected real devices including a Samsung Tab S9 FE+, and the customer whose landscape tablet originally reproduced the issue confirmed that the preview is now correct without the manual rotation workaround. Emulator behavior and a specialized always-landscape industrial display were separated for follow-up.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Version 0.6.14 leaves the same 90-degree rotation on all previously affected real devices.
The fix is verified on a different set of affected real phones and tablets, with the same correct orientation result.

edges.comment: Verification came from multiple affected participants, folded into one user side. A specialized naturally landscape industrial device remained a distinct follow-up rather than invalidating the broadly verified fix.

solution.intent: Ship the runtime-aware CameraX preview implementation that rebuilds when orientation changes and uses SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation to decide whether Flutter must apply rotation, then resolve the issue after affected users verify camera_android_camerax 0.6.14.
solution.concrete_example: Update to camera_android_camerax 0.6.14. Its preview widget responds to orientation-stream updates and checks SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation at runtime, applying a Flutter rotation only when the supplied Surface does not already handle crop and rotation.

edges.comment: PR flutter/packages#8629 landed in camera_android_camerax 0.6.14. The issue was closed after affected real-device users confirmed that the package-level fix removed their manual rotation requirement.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify both root causes: the preview widget was not rebuilt when orientation-stream updates arrived, and the plugin incorrectly used Android API level or presumed renderer behavior as a proxy for whether the SurfaceProducer already handled crop and rotation.

Must ground the diagnosis in the collected evidence: orientation or startup direction changes the failure, calculated orientation could update while the displayed Texture remained unchanged, renderer toggles and removing all correction produced inconsistent cross-device results, and the API 29 adjustment fixed only a subset.

Must prescribe the package-level runtime fix: rebuild the preview on orientation changes and consult SurfaceProducer.handlesCropAndRotation, applying Flutter-side rotation only when needed; the released vehicle is camera_android_camerax 0.6.14.

Must not close the case as a duplicate of the earlier Impeller-only issue, rely solely on an API-level or Impeller check, remove all rotation logic, or present a fixed RotatedBox quarter-turn as the general solution; each direction was contradicted by the thread's evidence.
Must keep rotated recorded-video playback and image metadata issues separate from this live CameraPreview issue.
Must declare resolution only after affected users verify the released fix on real devices; emulator-only results are insufficient.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter developer who can compare plugin implementations, pin transitive package versions, switch rendering configurations, reproduce on physical devices and emulators, and reason about CameraPreview transformations. Other affected developers with varied devices are folded into the same simulated user side.
persona_hint.communication_style: Technical, precise, persistent, and cooperative. Provides version boundaries and exact orientation steps, challenges premature duplicate closures with evidence, and tests proposed package builds while distinguishing live preview behavior from captured media playback.
